lines.text: A thousand people open the same page at once. All of them ask the database.
The database does the same work a thousand times.
Put a cache in front. A cache is a small, fast store of recent answers.
The first request misses. The cache asks the database, and keeps a copy.
The next requests hit. The cache answers right away. The database never hears about them.
If nine in ten requests hit the cache, the database sees one tenth of the load.
The catch: copies go stale. So each copy gets a time limit. When it runs out, the cache fetches a fresh one.
Fast reads, a quiet database, answers that are a little old. That is the trade.
